import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_98/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_98/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city' column (inner join by default)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# The target schema is ['city': string, 'fare': float]
# The joined table has columns: city, driver_count, type, date, fare, ride_id
# We only keep 'city' and 'fare' columns

# Convert 'city' to string explicitly (in case of any type issues)
joined["city"] = joined["city"].astype(str)

# Convert 'fare' to float explicitly
joined["fare"] = joined["fare"].astype(float)

# The target examples show no aggregation, but the joined table may have multiple rows per city.
# The target examples have unique city keys, so aggregate fare by average per city to match target distribution better.
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False)["fare"].mean()

# Sort by city to have consistent output (optional)
result = result.sort_values("city").reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the target path
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_98/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
